name: Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome
aliases: Orofacial granulomatosis with facial palsy and fissured tongue

criteria.description: Recurrent or persistent orofacial edema, especially of the lips
Histopathological evidence of non-caseating granulomatous inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two of the three major criteria (orofacial edema, facial palsy, fissured tongue) or one major criterion with supportive histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by biopsy; exclusion of other granulomatous diseases is essential

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
Exclusion of infectious and systemic granulomatous diseases
imaging: MRI may show facial nerve enhancement during palsy episodes
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible familial aggregation reported
other: Histopathology shows non-caseating granulomatous inflammation in affected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement including lungs and lymph nodes
Non-caseating granulomas on biopsy but with systemic signs
Gastrointestinal tract involvement with abdominal symptoms
Less frequent facial palsy and fissured tongue
Acute onset swelling without granulomatous inflammation
No facial palsy or fissured tongue
Often associated with allergic triggers or C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency

redFlags: Persistent or worsening orofacial swelling despite treatment
Signs of systemic granulomatous disease (e.g., pulmonary symptoms, lymphadenopathy)
references: Melkersson J, Rosenthal A. Recurrent facial paralysis, swelling of the lips, and fissured tongue: a syndrome. Acta Psychiatr Neurol Scand. 1931;6:1-20.
Worsaae N, Prause JU, Rasmussen PK. Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome: a review. J Oral Pathol Med. 1997;26(6):264-270.
